new_value: PARTLY STALE; residual fixed in 56efa94. The bead's two ordering problems: (1) the create_dir_all-under-umask half was already fixed -- server.rs prepare_socket_dir creates the directory 0700, tightens an owned directory that is too permissive, and refuses a directory another user owns. (2) The socket-mode window is real but unreachable, and the bead's own fix direction (umask around bind) was rejected: umask is per-process state shared by every thread, so setting and restoring it in an async daemon changes the mode of files other tokio workers create concurrently. The actual enforcement is the 0700 parent -- connect(2) needs search permission on it, and it exists before the socket does -- which is now recorded in the bind_listener doc comment. What WAS wrong and is now fixed: remove_file ran BEFORE prepare_socket_dir, so on the path where the daemon refuses a directory another user owns it had already unlinked a file inside it. Binding now prepares the directory first. Also fixed alongside: the stale-socket unlink was behind an exists() test, which follows symlinks and so reported false for a dangling symlink at the socket path; bind(2) then failed EADDRINUSE and the operator was told personad was already running. Three tests added, all mutation-verified (socket 0600, dir 0700, dangling symlink, and directory-vetted-before-unlink). The ordering test was VACUOUS on first writing -- it used /usr, where remove_file returns NotFound either way -- and was rewritten to use a parent that is a regular file, where the two orders give distinguishable errors.
